speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown
en: So control group is, "Don't touch it at all, leave it as it is."

speaker: Unknown

zh: 所以可重现性非常重要。

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

speaker: Unknown

zh: 它是在此基础上增加的。

speaker: Unknown
en: These are all new channels, so Google's slice of the pie stays the same, the pie gets bigger.
zh: 这些都是新渠道，所以 Google 的那块蛋糕保持不变，蛋糕变大了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so misinformation about Google going down, Google is not going down.
zh: 所以关于 Google 在走下坡路的错误信息，Google 并没有在走下坡路。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google published something recently, their VP of search explicitly said, "I looked at the traffic that we're sending to publishers, and it is not down, it's up slightly."
zh: Google 最近发布了一些东西，他们的搜索副总裁明确表示，“我看了一下我们发送给发布商的流量，并没有下降，而是略有上升。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So it is not true that Google Search is going down.
zh: 所以 Google 搜索在走下坡路并不是真的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And most of the news information about that is saying that it's going down, so that's the first surprising thing.
zh: 而且大多数关于这方面的新闻信息都说它在下降，所以这是第一个令人惊讶的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: The second surprising thing is tooling.
zh: 第二个令人惊讶的事情是工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I've never seen a channel where these extremely expensive tools that essentially do commodity tasks.
zh: 我从未见过这样一个渠道，这些极其昂贵的工具本质上执行的是大宗商品任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: So imagine if I said, "I'm going to charge you $50,000 for keyword tracking."
zh: 想象一下如果我说，“我要因为你进行关键词追踪而向你收取 50,000 美元。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You would say, "Well, of course, that's absurd.
zh: 你会说，“嗯，当然，这太荒谬了。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's keyword tracking, I could write this in a day."
zh: 这是关键词追踪，我一天就能写出来。”

speaker: Unknown
en: No one would do that.
zh: 没有人会那样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: But for answer engines, it's mysterious and people don't really know how it's working.
zh: 但对于答案引擎，它很神秘，人们并不真正知道它是如何工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, the slope of the growth curve is so significant, that I'm seeing people spend huge amounts of money on what are essentially keyword tracking commodities.
zh: 此外，增长曲线的斜率非常显著，我看到人们在本质上是大宗商品的关键词追踪工具上花费巨额资金。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's the second thing.
zh: 所以这是第二件事。

speaker: Unknown
en: The third thing is the growth curve of the channel.
zh: 第三件事是该渠道的增长曲线。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we did a Reforge AEO webinar a year ago, and there was excitement and then it died and there was very little excitement about it.
zh: 我们一年前做了一次 Reforge AEO 网络研讨会，当时有兴奋感，然后它消逝了，对此几乎没有兴奋感。

speaker: Unknown
en: This was in June, and then people didn't really care.
zh: 那是在六月，然后人们真的不在乎了。

speaker: Unknown
en: They were intrigued intellectually by it, but they didn't care because they didn't see the impact from that.
zh: 他们在理智上对它感到好奇，但他们不在乎，因为他们没有看到由此产生的影响。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there was essentially very little interest between July and January, and then suddenly in January it's just skyrocketing.
zh: 所以在七月到一月之间基本上几乎没有兴趣，然后突然在一月它就直线飙升。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's ChatGPT launches, people are very interested, and then it's not that interesting for growth people.
zh: 所以 ChatGPT 发布时，人们非常感兴趣，然后对于增长人员来说就没那么有趣了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there's this little spike in June, and then it's like this, which is usually not what you see with a new channel.
zh: 然后在六月有一个小高峰，然后就像这样，这通常不是你在新渠道上看到的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the slope of the curve is unusually steep, and the shape of the curve is also very unusual.
zh: 所以曲线的斜率异常陡峭，曲线的形状也非常不寻常。

speaker: Unknown
en: The last is that a lot of people do think that SEO and AEO are different and they're not different.
zh: 最后一点是，很多人确实认为 SEO 和 AEO 是不同的，而它们并没有不同。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think probably part of that is because it sounds great to say that there's this new channel, it's completely different.
zh: 我认为可能部分原因是因为说有一个新渠道、它完全不同听起来很棒。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm an expert and I have a tool to sell you, and it's totally unique and all these other tools are not relevant.
zh: 而且我是专家，我有一个工具要卖给你，它是完全独特的，所有其他工具都不相关。

speaker: Unknown
en: In reality, it's actually there's quite a bit of overlap.
zh: 在现实中，实际上有相当多的重叠。

speaker: Unknown
en: There is the difference of the citation optimization.
zh: 引文优化方面是有区别的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The head is different and the tail is different, but the core technology is pretty similar.
zh: 头部不同，尾部也不同，但核心技术非常相似。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are probably the most surprising things.
zh: 所以这些可能是最令人惊讶的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: This piece about January being the inflection point, you mentioned that it was because references started showing it more prominently.
zh: 关于一月是转折点这一点，你提到这是因为引用开始更显著地展示了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Is that the big change?
zh: 那是最大的变化吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: I think it's increase of adoption of LLMs by people, so it's just actually growing more and then the clickability.
zh: 我认为这是人们对 LLM 采用的增加，所以它实际上在增长更多，然后是可点击性。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I am seeing, you are seeing now this large increase of actual clicks.
zh: 我看到，你现在也看到实际点击的大幅增加。

speaker: Unknown
en: Probably before you got no clicks, even if you showed up an answer, so the clickability of the answer has increased.
zh: 以前你可能没有点击，即使你出现在答案中，所以答案的可点击性增加了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Especially for things like commerce and local and hotels, because they have these rich modules where you can click on stuff and go somewhere, which was not true before.
zh: 特别是对于商务、本地和酒店之类的东西，因为它们有这些丰富的模块，你可以点击东西并去某个地方，这以前是不真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That and I think people are just using LLMs more.
zh: 还有我认为人们只是更多地使用 LLM。

speaker: Unknown
en: Ethan, let me just say, I'm learning so much from this conversation, what a fun thing.
zh: Ethan，我只想说，我从这次对话中学到了很多东西，这真是一件有趣的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: I could see, it's just clear how much you love this stuff, and just how nerdy and deep you get into it.
zh: 我能看出来，很明显你是多么热爱这些东西，以及你是多么书呆子气和深入地研究它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's just fun to talk to someone that's so deep and knowledgeable about all these things, so thank you for sharing all this with us.
zh: 和一个对所有这些事情都有如此深入和知识渊博的人交谈真的很有趣，所以感谢你与我们分享所有这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: I'm going to go in a slightly different direction.
zh: 我要稍微换个方向。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's this whole world of AI content, people generating content with AI, generating landing pages.
zh: 有这整个 AI 内容的世界，人们用 AI 生成内容，生成落地页。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like, "Oh my God, SEO is never going to just generate all this stuff.
zh: 就像，“天哪，SEO 永远不会只生成所有这些东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is going to make all this stuff easier."
zh: AI 将使所有这些东西变得更容易。”

speaker: Unknown
en: You guys did a really big study on how that works, whether it's a good idea to generate content with AI.
zh: 你们做了一个关于它是如何工作的非常大的研究，用 AI 生成内容是不是一个好主意。

speaker: Unknown
en: Can you just talk about what you learned from that, and how people should think about AI in generating content?
zh: 你能谈谈你从中学到了什么，以及人们应该如何在生成内容中思考 AI 吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: Yes.
zh: 是的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I remember when ChatGPT launched and Brian Balfour posted on LinkedIn, "What do you people think that is going to happen from ChatGPT and AI?"
zh: 所以我记得当 ChatGPT 发布时，Brian Balfour 在 LinkedIn 上发帖，“你们这些人认为 ChatGPT 和 AI 会发生什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: And my immediate response is spam, so just lots and lots of spam, especially SEO spam.
zh: 我的直接回应是垃圾信息，所以只是大量的垃圾信息，特别是 SEO 垃圾信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then there was a whole industry around AI-generated content, and I knew immediately that it wouldn't work.
zh: 然后出现了一整个围绕 AI 生成内容的行业，我立刻就知道它不会奏效。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason why I knew it wouldn't work, and when I say AI-generated content, I mean automated content with no human-in-the-loop.
zh: 我知道它不会奏效的原因，当我说 AI 生成内容时，我指的是没有人工介入的自动化内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think that the future of content is clearly AI-assisted.
zh: 所以我认为内容的未来显然是 AI 辅助的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Clearly, you and I will be using AI to help us write, so it's not no AI at all, but it's not 100% generated with AI.
zh: 显然，你和我都会使用 AI 来帮助我们写作，所以并不是完全不用 AI，但这并不是 100% 由 AI 生成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I immediately knew that it wouldn't work.
zh: 我立刻就知道这行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did I know that?
zh: 我为什么知道那行不通？

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew that because I created spam in 2007, and I knew what Google did about it and how, and I knew the exact same thing was going to happen.
zh: 我知道那行不通是因为我在 2007 年制造过垃圾信息，而且我知道 Google 对此做了什么以及是如何做的，我知道完全相同的事情将会发生。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what I did in 2007 is I and all the other shopping comparison people scraped all each other's content, reviews, chopped it up, scraped content, 100 million search pages, snippets, and it worked really well.
zh: 所以我在 2007 年所做的是，我和所有其他的购物比较人员抓取了彼此的内容、评论，将其切碎，抓取内容，1 亿个搜索页面、片段，这效果非常好。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then it stopped working, and then all those companies disappeared.
zh: 然后它就不再起作用了，然后所有这些公司都消失了。

speaker: Unknown
en: I knew that was exactly what's going to happen with AI-generated content.
zh: 我知道这正是 AI 生成内容将会发生的事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so from the beginning, I've not focused on AI-generated content.
zh: 因此从一开始，我就没有专注于 AI 生成的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: Many people have, but I don't know, so maybe it does work.
zh: 许多人都专注于这个，但我不清楚，所以也许它确实有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's lots of case studies about it working.
zh: 关于它起作用有很多案例研究。

speaker: Unknown
en: So let's do the study, let's do an analysis.
zh: 所以让我们来做这项研究，让我们来做一个分析。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we took, we looked at both Google and at ChatGPT where we took thousands of searches and thousands of questions, and we put those searches into Google Search.
zh: 所以我们选取了，我们查看了 Google 和 ChatGPT，我们在那里选取了数千次搜索和数千个问题，我们将这些搜索放入 Google 搜索中。

speaker: Unknown
en: We put those questions into chat and the ChatGPT, and then we looked at the citations or the Google Search results.
zh: 我们把这些问题放入聊天和 ChatGPT 中，然后我们查看了引用或 Google 搜索结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then we looked at an AI detector.
zh: 然后我们查看了 AI 检测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we used Surfer SEO's AI detector.
zh: 所以我们使用了 Surfer SEO 的 AI 检测器。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, when I tell people this, they say, "Well, you can't detect AI."
zh: 现在，当我告诉人们这件事时，他们说，“嗯，你无法检测 AI。”

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we evaluated the efficacy and the accuracy of the AI detector.
zh: 所以然后我们评估了 AI 检测器的功效和准确性。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we did that by generating thousands of AI-generated articles and it was very predictive.
zh: 所以我们通过生成数千篇 AI 生成的文章来做到这一点，而且这是非常具有预测性的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we looked at real articles, we did that two different ways.
zh: 然后我们查看了真实的文章，我们分两种不同的方式进行了这项工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: One way is we write real articles, and the other is we took a random sample of 100,000 URLs from Common Crawl over the last five years.
zh: 一种方式是我们撰写真实的文章，另一种是我们从过去五年的 Common Crawl 中随机抽取了 10 万个 URL。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we looked at the AI detector before ChatGPT was launched, so it necessarily was content not created by a human.
zh: 然后我们查看了 ChatGPT 发布之前的 AI 检测器，所以那必然不是由人类创建的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then the false positive rate was around 8%, so basically the AI detector is very accurate.
zh: 然后误报率在 8% 左右，所以基本上 AI 检测器是非常准确的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we took that, then we ran it on the content.
zh: 所以我们采用了那个，然后我们在内容上运行了它。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then what we saw was around 10% to 12% of content in Google Search, and then ChatGPT or AI-generated, 90% are not.
zh: 所以我们观察到的是，Google 搜索中约有 10% 到 12% 的内容是 AI 生成的或 ChatGPT 生成的，90% 不是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we ran a correlation analysis showing the exact same thing.
zh: 我们运行了相关性分析，显示了完全相同的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we essentially did a very rigorous study showing that AI content does not work.
zh: 所以我们本质上做了一项非常严格的研究，表明 AI 内容行不通。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI-assisted content edited is great.
zh: AI 辅助的、经过编辑的内容是很棒的。

speaker: Unknown
en: We do that sometimes, other people do that, that is clearly the future of content.
zh: 我们有时会这样做，其他人也会这样做，这显然是内容的未来。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that does work and should work and that's good, but purely 100% AI-generated does not work.
zh: 所以这确实行得通，也应该行得通，这很好，但纯粹 100% AI 生成的不行。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then the second thing that we did was we found that, this was unexpected, but we found that there's more AI-generated content on the internet than human-generated content.
zh: 所以我们做的第二件事是，我们发现，这是出乎意料的，但我们发现互联网上的 AI 生成内容多于人类生成的内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So back to the Common Crawl study, we looked at 100,000 different URLs over the past five years.
zh: 回到 Common Crawl 研究，我们查看了过去五年中 10 万个不同的 URL。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you can see this curve where AI-generated is now higher than human-created.
zh: 然后你可以看到这条曲线，其中 AI 生成的现在高于人类创建的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So there's more AI-generated content on the internet than human-generated content, which is disturbing.
zh: 所以互联网上的 AI 生成内容多于人类生成的内容，这令人不安。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then let's say that AI-generated content did work.
zh: 所以让我们假设 AI 生成的内容确实有效。

speaker: Unknown
en: If AI-generated content worked, then everyone would do it.
zh: 如果 AI 生成的内容有效，那么每个人都会这样做。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just like in 2007, shopping comparison sites, if I can scrape my content, why would I pay anyone to write it?
zh: 就像在 2007 年，购物比较网站，如果我可以抓取我的内容，为什么要付钱给任何人来写它？

speaker: Unknown
en: I'll just scrape it from you and I'll chop it up.
zh: 我只会从你那里抓取它，然后我会把它切碎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then everyone will do that, and then it will go from most content is AI-generated to almost all of the content is AI-generated.
zh: 然后每个人都会这样做，然后它将从大多数内容是 AI 生成变为几乎所有的内容都是 AI 生成。

speaker: Unknown
en: Then what will happen if that works, is that Google now becomes a search engine for ChatGPT responses.
zh: 如果那行得通，接下来会发生的是，Google 现在变成了一个针对 ChatGPT 回答的搜索引擎。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if Google's a search engine for ChatGPT responses, there's no reason for Google to exist.
zh: 所以如果 Google 是一个针对 ChatGPT 回答的搜索引擎，Google 就没有理由存在了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Just go to ChatGPT, which is the exact same thing that happened in 2007.
zh: 直接去 ChatGPT 就好了，这与 2007 年发生的事情完全一样。

speaker: Unknown
en: Google said, "I see all these shopping comparison search engines showing up in my search results.
zh: Google 说，“我看到所有这些购物比较搜索引擎出现在我的搜索结果中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm essentially a search engine for search engines."
zh: 所以我本质上是一个搜索引擎的搜索引擎。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I should be showing the TV in my results.
zh: 我应该在我的结果中展示电视。

speaker: Unknown
en: I shouldn't be showing other vertical search engines, so I'm going to get rid of them and I'm just going to go straight to the product.
zh: 我不应该展示其他垂直搜索引擎，所以我要摆脱它们，我会直接跳转到产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: The same thing will be true for ChatGPT.
zh: 对于 ChatGPT 来说，同样的事情也会是真实的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now for ChatGPT, let's say that ChatGPT ranks its own derivatives in its citations, so then you have this infinite loop of derivatives.
zh: 现在对于 ChatGPT，假设 ChatGPT 将其衍生内容在其引用中排名，那么你就拥有了这个无限的衍生内容循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I go to ChatGPT, I say, "Generate 10 articles."
zh: 所以我进入 ChatGPT，我说，“生成 10 篇文章。”

speaker: Unknown
en: I put those articles into the citations and then I say, "Summarize these citations that were derivative."
zh: 我把这些文章放入引用中，然后我说，“总结这些属于衍生内容的引用。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And then I keep on doing derivatives of derivatives, and then you have an infinite loop of derivatives, and now AI is summarizing itself.
zh: 然后我不断做衍生内容的衍生内容，然后你有一个无限的衍生内容循环，现在 AI 正在总结它自己。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a paper about this called Model Collapse.
zh: 有一篇关于这个的论文叫做 Model Collapse。

speaker: Unknown
en: So again, there's the core algorithm and then there's the RAG piece.
zh: 所以再说一次，有核心算法，然后是 RAG 部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the core algorithm, a group did a study showing model collapse, which was what if you feed in AI derivatives into the model and train the core model on the derivatives?
zh: 所以核心算法，一个团队做了一项研究展示了模型崩溃，也就是如果你把 AI 衍生物喂给模型并在衍生品上训练核心模型会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then what happened was you had all these problems, hallucinations, things break very quickly.
zh: 然后发生的是你遇到了所有这些问题，幻觉，事情很快就会崩溃。

speaker: Unknown
en: Okay.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So then we did a study on what if you feed derivatives into the RAG piece?
zh: 所以然后我们做了一项研究，如果你把衍生品喂给 RAG 部分会怎样？

speaker: Unknown
en: So generate 10 derivatives, put that into RAG, summarize that.
zh: 所以生成 10 个衍生品，把它放进 RAG，总结它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then generate 10 more, and then summarize my summarizations, infinite loop of derivatives.
zh: 然后再生成 10 个，然后总结我的总结，衍生品的无限循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: What happens?
zh: 发生了什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what happens is there's a wisdom of the crowd.
zh: 所以发生的是有一种群体的智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: The LLM is summarizing the opinion of many people.
zh: LLM 正在总结许多人的意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you ask a question like, "What's the best flavor of ice cream?"
zh: 所以如果你问一个问题，比如“最好的冰淇淋口味是什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: There's not one answer, there's thousands of opinions.
zh: 没有一个答案，有数千种意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the LLM is summarizing these many, many opinions in this wisdom of the crowd.
zh: 所以 LLM 在这种群体的智慧中总结了这许多许多意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the wisdom of the crowd basically says that, "If you take the average of a large group of people, their average response will be better than the best single individual in the group."
zh: 群体的智慧基本上是说，“如果你取一大群人的平均值，他们的平均反应会比群体中最好的单个个体更好。”

speaker: Unknown
en: And so it's better to have more diversity of opinions, wisdom of the crowd.
zh: 所以拥有更多样化的意见更好，群体的智慧。

speaker: Unknown
en: So what happens to the infinite loop of derivatives?
zh: 那么衍生品的无限循环会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: You essentially converge on one opinion.
zh: 你基本上会收敛到一个意见。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you ask, "What's the best flavor of ice cream?"
zh: 所以如果你问，“最好的冰淇淋口味是什么？”

speaker: Unknown
en: It will eventually say, "It's vanilla and it's only vanilla, and there's no other flavor of ice cream."
